about.authorPS:
This UI framework was written by the author while developing projects, frustrated that the uni-app x plugin market lacked a UI library that suited his needs.
　　I work on many projects, most of them small, and my budget is not particularly generous. For small personal projects, licensing fees for a more polished UI framework are relatively high and simply not cost-effective. Most free UI frameworks don't quite match the style of my projects, so I wrote my own.
　　Since I'm often still in school, the update frequency depends on the situation. If it doesn't meet your needs, you are welcome to do your own secondary development.

otherUi.firstui:
FirstUI, a lightweight, simple, efficient, and comprehensive mobile component library that adapts to uni-app x.
　　Among the open-source UI frameworks in the uni-app x plugin market, it is considered fairly polished, and its components are quite rich.
otherUi.naiveui:
A Vue 3 component library with over 90 components, fairly complete, themeable, and fully written in TypeScript.
　　This UI framework's initial design philosophy also drew from it; in some of SinleUI's components you can see its influence.
otherUi.title: UI Framework Recommendations
otherUi.tmui:
Also known as XUI, built with native UTS development for stability, efficiency, performance, and exquisite aesthetics. It is the next-generation successor of tmui3.0 and won first prize in the official UTS plugin competition in 2023.
　　In my experience it is the most refined UI library in the uni-app x plugin market so far, with excellent taste, fairly complete functional components, and an ideal choice for commercial application frameworks.
otherUi.uview:
uView is a uni-app ecosystem framework fully compatible with nvue, whose comprehensive components and convenient tools will help you get things done with ease.
　　Needless to say, it's absolutely the backbone of uni-app—unfortunately it doesn't support Vue3.
otherUi.uvui:
uv-ui is a feature-rich UI framework based on uni-app, with some components based on uView2.x, fully cross-end compatible, supporting standalone import. It is compatible with vue3+2, app, h5, mini-programs and more, ready to use out of the box.
　　As uView's successor, it supports Vue3 and builds on it further. If you are building apps with uni-app, it is highly recommended.
otherUi.uxframe:
Winner of the first prize in the 2023 plugin competition, it is a low-code, high-performance native UI framework based on the uni-app x cross-platform application development engine.
　　It is currently the highest-performing UI library in the uni-app x plugin market; if you pursue performance to the extreme, it may satisfy you.

snText.memorialAddr: The late emperor founded his enterprise only to pass away mid-way; today the realm is divided into three, and Yi province is weary and weak — truly a critical moment of survival. Yet courtiers remain diligent within, and loyal scholars forget themselves outside, in pursuit of the late emperor's special grace, wishing to repay your Majesty. Truly you should broaden your sage ear to glorify the late emperor's virtue and revive the spirit of determined men; you should not belittle yourself, or use poor metaphors that block the path of loyal remonstrance. The palace and the government are one body; reward and punishment should not differ. If anyone commits crimes or does good, they should be handed to the proper officials to decide punishment and reward, to manifest your Majesty's impartial rule, and you should not play favorites so that inside and outside follow different laws.

tabbarSub1.baiJuYiDesc: Bai Juyi (772–846), courtesy name Letian, one of the "Three Great Poets" of the Tang dynasty. With Yuan Zhen he championed the New Yuefu movement (the "Yuan–Bai" pair); with Liu Yuxi he was the "Liu–Bai" pair. His poetry ranges widely in theme and form with plain, accessible language, earning him the titles "Poetry Devil" and "Poetry King". He rose to Hanlin Academician and the office of Left Zan-shan Grand Master. His Bai Shi Changqing Ji survives; representative works include "Song of Everlasting Regret", "The Old Charcoal Seller" and "Pipa Xing".
tabbarSub1.duFuDesc: Du Fu (712–770), courtesy name Zimei, reverently called the "Sage of Poetry"; his poems are called "poetic history". A great Realist poet of the Tang dynasty, paired with Li Bai as the "Li–Du" duo. Deeply patriotic and noble in character, over 1,400 of his poems survive; his refined craft is held in high regard in classical Chinese poetry. He lived in Chengdu from 759 to 766, commemorated by the Du Fu Thatched Cottage.
tabbarSub1.liBaiDesc: Li Bai (701–762), courtesy name Taibai, known as the "Immortal Poet". A great Romantic poet of the Tang dynasty, celebrated alongside Du Fu as the "Li–Du" pair. A descendant of the imperial Li clan, he was boisterous and generous, loved wine and poetry, and cherished friendship. Deeply influenced by Taoist thought, his collected works Li Taibai Ji survive; many poems were written while drunk, including "Viewing the Waterfall at Mount Lu", "Hard Is the Road to Shu", "Invitation to Wine" and others.
tabbarSub1.liQingZhaoDesc: Li Qingzhao (1084–1155), titled Yi'an Jushi, was a Song-dynasty poet and the leading figure of the wanyue (graceful) ci school, hailed as the "foremost talented woman in a thousand years". Her early ci depict a serene life; later works lament her circumstances with a melancholy tone. She excelled in plain, delicate description, urged that ci must follow musical rules and elegance, and argued that ci is "a separate genre" distinct from shi poetry. Some of her poems survive; the Yi'an Jushi Anthology is lost, but the Shu Yu Ci collection was compiled later, and a critical edition Li Qingzhao Collection exists today.
tabbarSub1.liShangYinDesc: Li Shangyin (813–858), courtesy name Yishan, a leading poet of the late Tang. With Du Mu he formed the "Little Li–Du" pair and with Wen Tingyun the "Wen–Li" pair. His poetry is inventive in conception and rich in style; his love poems and "untitled" poems, lingering and beautiful, are widely recited, though some are too obscure to parse. Stuck between the Niu and Li factional strife, he never fulfilled his ambition. He was buried in his hometown Qinyang (Henan); his works are collected in the Li Yishan Poems.
tabbarSub1.suShiDesc: Su Shi (1037–1101), known as Su Dongpo, was a celebrated literary figure of the Northern Song and an influencer in water management. A leading writer of mid-Northern Song, he excelled in poetry, ci, prose, calligraphy and painting. With Huang Tingjian he formed the "Su–Huang" pair; with Xin Qiji he represented the unconstrained haofang school ("Su–Xin"); with Ouyang Xiu he was the "Ou–Su" pair, one of the "Eight Great Prose Masters of Tang and Song". A renowned calligrapher and one of "Four Song Masters", he was especially skilled in ink bamboo, grotesque rocks and withered trees. Works include the Dongpo Qi Ji, Dongpo Yuefu and scroll paintings like Xiao Xiang Bamboo and Stone.
tabbarSub1.title: Home
tabbarSub1.wangWeiDesc: Wang Wei (701–761), courtesy name Mojie, was a Tang poet honored as the "Buddha of Poetry". Su Shi praised him: "poetry in his paintings, painting in his poetry". A representative poet of the High Tang, more than 400 of his poems survive, including "Acacia" and "Autumn Dusk in the Mountains". Deeply versed in Buddhism and influenced by Zen, his names derive from the Vimalakirti Sutra. Famous in poetry, calligraphy and painting and talented in music, he formed the "Wang–Meng" pair with Meng Haoran.
tabbarSub1.xinQiJiDesc: Xin Qiji (1140–1207), courtesy name You'an, was a Southern Song official, general and writer, one of the leading ci poets of the haofang (bold) school, called the "Dragon among Ci". Paired with Su Shi as "Su–Xin" and with Li Qingzhao as the "Two Ans of Jinan". Born when the Central Plains had fallen to the Jin, he joined the anti-Jin army at 21 and later served the Southern Song, advocating resistance all his life, submitting the Mei Qin Ten Essays and Nine Views on military strategy. His ci express patriotic fervor for reunification, the grief of unfulfilled ambition, and sharp criticism of appeasement, with many pieces praising the motherland's rivers and mountains.
tabbarSub2.baiJuYiDesc: Bai Juyi, courtesy name Letian, titled Xiangshan Jushi. One of the "Three Great Poets" of the Tang dynasty; with Yuan Zhen the "Yuan–Bai" pair and with Liu Yuxi the "Liu–Bai" pair. His poetry has broad themes, varied forms and plain, accessible language, earning him the titles "Poetry Devil" and "Poetry King".
tabbarSub2.duFuDesc: Du Fu, courtesy name Zimei, called himself Shaoling Yelao, known as "Du Gongbu". A great Realist poet of the Tang dynasty, revered as the "Sage of Poetry" with poems called "poetic history", forming the "Li–Du" pair with Li Bai.
tabbarSub2.liBaiDesc: Li Bai, courtesy name Taibai, titled Qinglian Jushi, also called the "Banished Immortal". A great Romantic poet of the Tang dynasty, hailed as the "Immortal Poet" and paired with Du Fu as the "Li–Du" duo.
tabbarSub2.liQingZhaoDesc: Li Qingzhao, titled Yi'an Jushi. A Song-dynasty poet and the leading figure of the wanyue ci school, called the "foremost talented woman in a thousand years". Her early ci are serene, later ones mournful; she argued that ci is "a separate genre" with its own musical rules and elegance.
tabbarSub2.liShangYinDesc: Li Shangyin, courtesy name Yishan. A famous Tang poet and one of the best of the late Tang; the "Little Li–Du" pair with Du Mu and the "Wen–Li" pair with Wen Tingyun. His poetry is inventive, rich in style and beautifully moving, widely recited.
tabbarSub2.suShiDesc: Su Shi, courtesy names Zizhan and Hezhong, known as Su Dongpo and "Su the Immortal". A famous Northern Song writer, calligrapher and painter, and a noted water-management official; the "Su–Huang", "Su–Xin" and "Ou–Su" pairings, one of the "Eight Great Prose Masters of Tang and Song".

A representative High Tang poet versed in Buddhism and influenced by Zen; famous in calligraphy and painting, talented in music; the "Wang–Meng" pair with Meng Haoran.

watermarkFull.desc: The watermark covers the whole page; touch events pass through so nothing is blocked, and all controls below work normally
watermarkFull.line1: The watermark layer is on top, but pointer-events: none lets touch events pass through,
watermarkFull.line2: so buttons, switches, swipes and other interactions on the page are unaffected.
watermarkFull.line3: When the content is shorter than one screen, the watermark area at least fills the viewport height (min-height),
watermarkFull.line4: and when the content overflows, the whole page scrolls and the watermark covers the content as it goes.
watermarkFull.line5: Multi-line text watermarks, color, font size, spacing and rotation angle can all be adjusted freely.
